title: How diamond clarity is graded
topic: diamond clarity grades gia scale eleven flawless internally flawless vvs vs si i1 i3 10x magnification inclusions blemishes five factors size number position center of the top eye clean look alike

lines.text: Clarity counts inclusions inside the stone and blemishes on its surface.
The GIA scale runs from Flawless down to I3.
lines.say: The GEE eye AY scale runs from Flawless down to eye three.

lines.text: Flawless means no inclusions or blemishes are visible at 10x.
lines.say: Flawless means no inclusions or blemishes are visible at ten times.

lines.text: Internally Flawless allows surface blemishes but no visible inclusions.
At 10x, VVS inclusions are hard for a skilled grader to see.
lines.say: At ten times, vee vee ess inclusions are hard for a skilled grader to see.

lines.text: Graders weigh five factors, starting with size and number.
An inclusion near the center of the top affects the grade more.
Many are too small to see, which is why graders magnify.
Neighboring VVS and VS diamonds usually look alike to the eye.
lines.say: Neighboring vee vee ess and vee ess diamonds usually look alike to the eye.

lines.text: A render shows the diamond in the design before it is made.

post.youtube_title: Jewelry render basics: how diamond clarity is graded
post.caption: Diamond clarity has eleven grades on the GIA scale, from Flawless down to I3. Graders look at inclusions inside the stone and blemishes on its surface, judge them at 10x, and weigh five factors, including how close a flaw sits to the center of the top. Neighboring VVS and VS diamonds usually look alike to the eye. A render shows the diamond in the design before it is made. The renders in this video were made with HeyGema.
